newsitem.title: SYRIA: Lebanon's Bouez accuses Israel of raising tension.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Bouez accuses Israel of raising tension.

text.p: Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez on Wednesday accused Israel of increasing tension in south Lebanon and trying to undermine security in Syria and Lebanon.
Talking to Reuters after meeting Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara in Damascus, Bouez said Syria and Lebanon were still committed to the peace process.
"We discussed the Israeli escalation in south Lebanon and the security operations which aim at shaking the internal ranks of Syria and Lebanon," Bouez said.

He was referring to the bombing of a bus in Damascus on New Year's Eve that killed 11 people and wounded 42, and an attack on a bus carrying Syrian workers in Lebanon last month which killed the Syrian driver and wounded others.
Syria accused Israeli agents of responsibility for the bus bombing and Lebanon said Christian hardliners linked with Israel were responsible for the Lebanon attack. Israel denied the accusations.
Syria is the main foreign power broker in Lebanon where it has some 35,000 troops.
"The Israeli government is resorting to this method because of the embarrassment it is suffering from as a result of the suspension of the peace talks," Bouez said.
He said Israel wanted Syria and Lebanon to abandon the peace process but added: "We are continuing the peace process in full coordination with Syria. We could never be removed from this framework."
Syria and Lebanon have held sporadic peace talks since 1991 but no breakthrough was achieved.

Both countries have condemned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for refusing to swap occupied Arab land for peace and said no talks would be held until he accepted the principle of withdrawal.

Bouez's visit to Syria followed increased military operations in south Lebanon by Israeli troops and militias of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah Shi'ite group fighting the Israeli presence in south Lebanon.
